rounds.text: Jujhar Logistics Limited is trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a discounted cash flow model placing the intrinsic value at Rs 573 per share against a market price of Rs 239, which leaves an attractive margin of safety of 58.3% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price only prices in a modest 6.0% earnings growth, whereas the base case assumes an 18.0% growth rate [E45]. The company's underlying fundamentals are vastly outpacing its stock price, highlighted by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 195% compared to a share price growth of 63%, and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 756% alongside exceptional sales growth [E16, E19, E21, E54]. Profitability and capital efficiency metrics strongly outperform sector benchmarks, with a Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of 25.14% against a sector benchmark of 12.66%, and an EV/EBITDA of 8.7x compared to the sector benchmark of 14.08x [E10, E11]. Operational quality is also surging, demonstrated by debtor days improving from 81.7 to 44.8 days and operating cash flow reaching Rs 35 Cr in March 2026, backed by high cash conversion [E32, E33, E58]. Conceded: free cash flow was Rs -68 Cr in March 2026 [E34].

Despite recent high-growth metrics, the business carries severe historical underperformance and severe cash burn risks that the current valuation fails to fully price in [E24, E34]. The company's median return on equity over 10 years sits at a meager 2%, and over a 5-year period it drops further into negative territory at -3% [E24, E25]. This poor long-term structural profitability is compounded by a high price-to-book ratio of 4.07x against a book value of ₹ 58.7, which exceeds the sector benchmark price-to-book of 2.61x [E2, E7, E59]. Furthermore, despite reporting strong operating cash flow of Rs 35 Cr in March 2026, the company generated a massive negative free cash flow of Rs -68 Cr during the same period, while borrowings surged to Rs 21 Cr from Rs 6 Cr a year earlier [E33, E34, E38]. The investment case is also burdened by high volatility of 59.1% and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -79.2%, alongside decelerating earnings growth flagged by screening rules [E51, E52, E66]. Conceded: the company displays a strong trailing twelve months profit growth of 756% and a high operating margin of 21% [E19, E28].

Conceded: historical return on equity over 10 and 5 years reflects past periods of weakness [E24, E25]. However, the business has undergone a structural transformation, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 756% and a recent median return on equity of 17% [E19, E27]. While the price-to-book ratio is 4.07x [E2], this premium is justified by an exceptional return on capital employed of 25.14% compared to the sector benchmark of 12.66% [E10] and a low EV/EBITDA of 8.7x versus a sector benchmark of 14.08x [E11]. The negative free cash flow of Rs -68 Cr in March 2026 [E34] is contextualized by robust operating cash flow of Rs 35 Cr [E33], strong cash conversion of 4.38x [E32], and a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 12.03x [E37]. Furthermore, the surging borrowings to Rs 21 Cr [E38] remain backed by a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.41x [E36] and rising promoter confidence, with insider holdings increasing by 11.65 percentage points to 73.75% [E40]. Finally, the fundamental momentum significantly outpaces the share price appreciation, with 5-year profit growth at 195% against a price growth of 63% [E54], operating margins expanding dramatically by 20 percentage points [E28], and a high relative strength rating of 100 [E49].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 756% and recent median return on equity hit 17% [E19, E27]. However, the bull's dismissal of the historical track record glosses over a median return on equity of 2% over 10 years and -3% over 5 years, alongside a low 3-year average of 6.69% [E24, E25, E60]. The premium 4.07x price-to-book valuation sits well above the sector benchmark of 2.61x and is specifically flagged as a negative in the filed statements [E2, E7, E59]. While operating cash flow reached Rs 35 Cr, free cash flow deteriorated sharply to Rs -68 Cr, and borrowings surged from Rs 6 Cr to Rs 21 Cr in a single year [E33, E34, E38]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is quietly retreating rather than rising, with domestic institutional holdings dropping from 2.11% to 0.70% [E41]. Finally, the rules-based screen explicitly warns that earnings growth is decelerating and operating margins are inconsistent over the last two years and two quarters [E30, E31, E66].

Conceded: domestic institutional holdings dropped from 2.11% to 0.70% [E41], and free cash flow deteriorated to Rs -68 Cr alongside a rise in borrowings to Rs 21 Cr [E34, E38]. However, the bear's fixation on historical multi-year median ROE figures of 2% and -3% [E24, E25] ignores the inflection into a robust 17% last-year median [E27] and an impressive 25.14% ROCE that handily beats the 12.66% sector benchmark [E10]. While the price-to-book of 3.96x exceeds the sector median [E7], it is completely justified by a phenomenal 195% 5-year profit growth [E17] and a TTM operating margin that expanded by 20 percentage points to 21% [E28]. Conceded: operating margins are flagged as inconsistent [E30, E31], but this volatility is overshadowed by exceptional fundamental velocity including a TTM sales surge of 607% [E16] and profit growth of 756% [E19] that dramatically outpaces the company's 63% 5-year share price growth [E21]. Finally, the rules-based screen scoring 85 out of 100 with a BUY confidence rating confirms that the overarching fundamentals far outweigh the short-term noise cited [E61].

Conceded: TTM sales surged 607% [E16] and profit growth reached 756% [E19]. However, this extreme short-term velocity clashes with the rules-based screening warnings that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E66]. The bull defends the rich valuation by pointing to the 5-year profit growth [E17], yet glosses over the historical record of a median 10-year ROE of 2% and a 5-year median ROE of -3% [E24, E25], which contextualizes why the company carries a low 3-year median ROE of 6.69% [E60]. While ROCE stands at a strong 25.14% [E10], the company trades at an elevated price-to-book multiple of 3.96x to 4.07x against a sector benchmark of just 2.61x [E2, E7]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes the flagged operating-margin inconsistency [E30, E31] as short-term noise, but ignores the severe cash drain revealed by a negative free cash flow of Rs -68 Cr and a tripling of borrowings to Rs 21 Cr [E34, E38]. Finally, the institutional backing is quietly retreating as domestic institutions slashed their stake to 0.70% [E41], signaling a lack of smart-money conviction behind the screen's buy rating.
